correctness.rationale: The conserved-mass magnetization law in the motivating source gives \(\dot m=-2m^3/3-m^5/15+O(m^7)\). The reciprocal-square substitution \(u=m^{-2}\) yields \(m(t)=\sqrt3/(2\sqrt t)+O((\log t)/t^{3/2})\) and the sharp integrals \(\int_1^t m(s)\,ds=\sqrt3\sqrt t+C+o(1)\) and \(\int_1^t m(s)^2\,ds=(3/4)\log t+C\prime+o(1)\). The exact fixed Fourier matrix has eigenvalues \(-\cosh m\pm\sqrt{1+(\sinh m-ik)^2}\). For every unit-torus nonzero Fourier wave number \(k=2\pi n>1\), the dominant eigenvalue has real part \(-1+(k/\sqrt{k^2-1})m-m^2/2+O(m^3)\). Its analytic eigenbasis has integrable derivative coupling of order \(t^{-3/2}\); forward and backward invariant Riccati graphs are order \(t^{-1}\), yielding precisely one exceptional complex fast-solution subspace and a finite nonzero generic slow prefactor. Integration gives \(t^{-3/8}\exp[-t+\sqrt3k\sqrt t/\sqrt{k^2-1}]\). At zero initial magnetization the mode matrix is constant with eigenvalues \(-1\pm i\sqrt{k^2-1}\). Symbolic checks and numerical integration to time 2000 support but do not prove the infinite-time claim.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2025 primary preprint establishes the PDE and nonlinear mean-field magnetization law, but its theorem is a hydrodynamic fixed-time limit and its large-deviation analysis does not yield a fixed spatial Fourier t→∞ asymptotic. The 2024 stationary-fluctuation paper assumes internal switching rates independent of magnetization, studies Gaussian fluctuations and covariance rather than deterministic nonstationary critical spatial relaxation. The 2021 exact two-state Fourier/Laplace formula is for constant switching and stationary internal Markov dynamics, not time-evolving self-consistent Curie--Weiss flip rates. General 2×2 asymptotic integration is established mathematical technique but does not supply the coefficient and logarithmic exponent for this specified PDE without analysis. Actual claim/source-alias searches in published-finding corpus returned only different models, most notably a 5-dimensional Lorenz critical correction and a convective Chafee–Infante critical relaxation, neither of which implies the statement. No universal originality guarantee is inferred.

value.rationale: At the natural Curie–Weiss alignment threshold \(\beta=1\), global order relaxes algebraically whereas each nonzero spatial inhomogeneity mode relaxes exponentially with a computable square-root exponent enhancement and a universal power \(t^{-3/8}\). The mode-dependent coefficient and exact one-dimensional exceptional channel determine a structural critical response, quantifying homogenization beyond the magnetization alone. The unit torus gives every nonzero frequency above the spectral threshold, so this is a natural whole-family statement and not an arbitrary parameter slice.
